name: Whiskey Sour
tagline: Tart, smooth and a little bit sweet.
intro: The Whiskey Sour pairs bourbon with lemon and a touch of sweetness. It's balanced, bright and easy to drink, with the whiskey still clearly in front. It's also a great starting point if you're new to whiskey cocktails.
heroAlt: Engraved line illustration of a Whiskey Sour with citrus and a cherry

glassware.name: Rocks glass
glassware.note: Serve over ice. Use a coupe if you'd like it up.

ingredients.note: A 90 to 100 proof bourbon holds up well to the lemon.
Equal parts sugar and water, stirred until dissolved.

steps.title: Chill the glass
steps.body: Fill a rocks glass with ice to chill it while you mix.

steps.title: Combine the ingredients
steps.body: Add the bourbon, lemon juice and simple syrup to a shaker.

steps.title: Shake with ice
steps.body: Fill the shaker with ice and shake hard for 12 to 15 seconds. You want the shaker to feel frosty cold, which means the drink is chilled and diluted well.

steps.title: Strain
steps.body: Dump the ice from your glass and add fresh ice. Strain the drink over it.
steps.tip: For a silkier texture, strain through a fine mesh strainer as well.

steps.title: Garnish
steps.body: Add a lemon wheel, and a cherry if you like. Taste, and adjust your next round to suit your preference.

tips: Pro tip: Make your simple syrup in advance. It keeps in the fridge for about two weeks.
Pro tip: For a fuller foam, try a dry shake first: shake without ice, then shake again with ice.
Common mistake: Using bottled lemon juice or sour mix, which tastes flat and overly sweet.
Common mistake: Not shaking long enough. The drink should be very cold with a soft, rounded edge.

variations.name: New York Sour
variations.description: Float about ½ oz of dry red wine on top for color and a tannic edge.

variations.name: Boston Sour
variations.description: Add egg white to the shaker for a silky texture and thick foam, using the dry shake method.

variations.name: Gold Rush
variations.description: Replace the simple syrup with honey syrup and use lemon juice.

variations.name: Rye Whiskey Sour
variations.description: Use rye in place of bourbon for a spicier, drier version.

substitutions: Bourbon: Rye whiskey or a smooth blended whiskey also work well.
Simple syrup: Honey syrup (equal parts honey and warm water) or maple syrup adds richer flavor.
Lemon juice: Fresh lime makes a tarter drink, similar to a whiskey daiquiri.
history: Sours, a family of drinks made from spirit, citrus and sugar, were well established by the mid-1800s. The Whiskey Sour appears in Jerry Thomas's 1862 bartender's guide.

seo.title: Whiskey Sour Recipe: Bourbon, Lemon and Simple Syrup
seo.description: Make a classic Whiskey Sour with 2 oz bourbon, ¾ oz lemon juice and ¾ oz simple syrup. Easy steps, tips and variations.
